rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for marking the endpoint of a time period or a place in everyday Cantonese.

example.english: We will wait until six o’clock before leaving.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 dang2 dou3 luk6 dim2 sin1 zau2

rows.note: Use this mainly in formal or written wording for an endpoint in time or at a place.

example.english: The event will be postponed until next week.
example.traditional: 活動將延至下星期舉行。
example.jyutping: wut6 dung6 zoeng1 jin4 zi3 haa6 sing1 kei4 geoi2 hang4

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial pattern for saying that B happens only once A has happened.

example.english: We won't eat until you get back.
example.jyutping: dou3 nei5 faan1 lei4 sin1 sik6 faan6

rows.note: Use this when the main action is deliberately delayed while waiting for A.

example.english: We'll wait until the rain stops before going out.
example.jyutping: dang2 dou3 jyu5 ting4 sin1 ceot1 gaai1

rows.note: Use this, especially in more careful speech or writing, to emphasize that B did not happen before A.

example.english: The results will not be announced until the manager approves them.
example.traditional: 直到經理批准先公布結果。
example.jyutping: zik6 dou3 ging1 lei5 pai1 zeon2 sin1 gung1 bou3 git3 gwo2

rows.note: Use this for an explicit endpoint when something continues up to the time A becomes true.

example.english: The venue will have people there until midnight.
example.traditional: 直到午夜為止，會場都有人。
example.jyutping: zik6 dou3 ng5 je6 wai4 zi2 wui5 coeng4 dou1 jau5 jan4
